_about.purpose: Fixed question set for measuring retrieval quality. Written from the source documents, never from retrieval output - a test shaped to fit the system measures nothing.
_about.scoring: expect_sections lists the section ids that must be retrieved for the answer to be possible. Retrieval is scored on whether they appear, which needs no model and costs nothing.
_about.wording_note: Some questions deliberately use everyday English and some use terms of art. The Act's vocabulary differs from ordinary usage - 'supervise' means market surveillance, not human oversight - so wording is a variable worth measuring, not one to control away.

categories.direct: answer sits in one section of the Act
categories.cross_ref: answer spans sections linked by the Act's own citations
categories.other_source: answer sits in one non-Act document (NIST or OWASP)
categories.out_of_corpus: no document here can answer it; the system should decline

_about.provenance: Answer keys were written from the source documents and committed before any run. The git history is the evidence.

questions.question: What are the fines for breaking the AI Act?
questions.notes: Penalties. Article 101 covers GPAI fines separately.

questions.question: What must the technical documentation for a high-risk AI system contain?
questions.notes: Article 11 imposes the duty; Annex IV lists the contents.

questions.question: Does the law require AI systems to keep logs?
questions.notes: Record-keeping. Article 19 covers retention of automatically generated logs.

questions.question: Can an ordinary person complain about an AI system, and to whom?
questions.notes: Right to lodge a complaint with a market surveillance authority.

questions.question: How does the Regulation define an AI system?
questions.notes: Article 3(1). Article 3 is 12 chunks, so this also tests whether the right part surfaces.

questions.question: What obligations apply to providers of general-purpose AI models?
questions.notes: GPAI regime is separate from the high-risk regime - a common confusion.

questions.question: When does the AI Act actually start applying?
questions.notes: Entry into force and staggered application.

questions.question: What are the rules for affixing the CE marking to an AI system?
If an AI system makes a decision about me, can I demand an explanation?
questions.notes: Right to explanation of individual decision-making.

questions.question: What does the Act require regarding accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity?
questions.notes: Near-verbatim title match. Should be the easiest question in the set - a floor.

questions.question: Does the EU AI Act apply to a company based in the United States?
questions.notes: Added after the baseline run. Known to fail: retrieval returns Article 2 part 7 of 10 (research exclusions) rather than part 1 (extraterritorial scope). The right article, the wrong chunk - a failure mode the original 25 did not cover. Article 2(1) applies the Regulation to providers in a third country placing systems on the Union market, and to third-country providers and deployers where the output is used in the Union.

questions.question: Is my CV screening tool for hiring considered high-risk?
questions.notes: The flagship case. Article 6 defines high-risk by pointing at Annex III; the employment category is Annex III item 4.

questions.question: Who is responsible for human oversight of a high-risk AI system, and what must that person be able to do?
questions.notes: Article 14 sets the requirement; Article 26 makes the deployer assign it.

questions.question: When is a general-purpose AI model considered to pose systemic risk?
questions.notes: Article 51 classifies; Annex XIII gives the designation criteria.

questions.question: What AI uses are banned outright, and does that connect to any list of crimes?
questions.notes: Article 5 prohibits; Annex II lists the criminal offences it refers to.

questions.question: How long does a provider have to keep documentation, and what documentation is it?
questions.notes: Article 18 sets the retention period; Article 11 defines what is retained.

questions.question: What conformity assessment procedure applies to a high-risk AI system listed in Annex III?
questions.notes: Article 43 routes to the annexes; Annex VI is internal control.

questions.question: What information has to be registered in the EU database before a high-risk system goes live?
questions.notes: Article 49 requires registration; Annex VIII lists the fields. Article 71 covers the database itself.

questions.question: How does the Act's risk management requirement compare with the NIST AI Risk Management Framework?
questions.notes: Needs Article 9 plus any NIST section. Scored on both sources appearing, since NIST has no single canonical section for this.

questions.question: What can go wrong with the embeddings and vector search in a retrieval system?
questions.notes: OWASP LLM09. The system being asked about the risks of how it is itself built.

questions.question: What are the four core functions of the NIST AI Risk Management Framework?
questions.notes: Govern, Map, Measure, Manage.

questions.question: What is prompt injection and why is it hard to defend against?
questions.notes: OWASP LLM01.

questions.question: What does ISO/IEC 42001 require for certification, and what does it cost?
questions.notes: ISO is paywalled and deliberately excluded. The system should decline, not improvise from adjacent material.

questions.question: What are the penalties under the Colorado AI Act?
questions.notes: US state law, not in the corpus. Tempting to answer from the EU penalties article.

questions.question: What do the recitals say about the intent behind the high-risk classification rules?
questions.notes: Tests the known limitation: EUR-Lex consolidated texts carry operative text only, so this corpus holds no recitals. The system must not answer from the articles as though they were recitals.

questions.question: How many companies have been fined under the AI Act so far?
questions.notes: A factual question about the world, not about the text. No document can answer it.

questions.question: Can we use sensitive personal data like ethnicity to check whether our AI system is biased?
questions.notes: Article 4a, inserted by the July 2026 amendment. Nothing else in the set touches the six amendment-only articles, so nothing tested the property that distinguishes this corpus from the superseded 2024 text. Plain wording against 'special categories of personal data' also makes it a vocabulary test.

questions.question: Can the AI Office itself impose fines, and on whom?
questions.notes: Article 75c, also amendment-only. Deliberately hard: Article 99 (Penalties) and Article 101 (fines for GPAI providers) are both plausible and both wrong. Tests whether three fine regimes can be told apart.

questions.question: If we want to test our high-risk AI system on real people before launch, what are the rules?
questions.notes: Article 60 covers real-world testing; Article 60a, added in 2026, covers products already under Union harmonisation legislation. Tests whether an amendment surfaces alongside the provision it supplements.

questions.question: What does the Act require for cybersecurity of high-risk systems, and what attacks should we actually defend against?
questions.notes: Genuinely two-document: Article 15 states the obligation, OWASP supplies the concrete threats. Before this, C01 was the only question requiring two sources.
